# Maximize Pair Strength Using GCD.

@example 20 and 30 have gcd 10, for a strength of 2 * 3 = 6. 7 shares no divisor but 1 with either, so 20 and 7 give 140, and 30 and 7 give 210.
[20,30,7]
=> 210

@example 14 and 21 have gcd 7, so their strength is 2 * 3 = 6. 21 and 6 have gcd 3, giving 7 * 2 = 14. 14 and 6 have gcd 2, giving 7 * 3 = 21.
[14,21,6]
=> 21

@example The two 12s sit at different indices, so they may be paired, but equal values give only 1. Either 12 with 4 gives 3 * 1 = 3.
[12,4,12]
=> 3

# The smallest input.
[1,1]
=> 1

# Two values: 2 divides 4, so the strength is the quotient.
[2,4]
=> 2

# 1 paired with x gives x.
[1,100000]
=> 100000

# Two large values with no common divisor: past 2^31 - 1.
[100000,99999]
=> 9999900000

# The two equal largest values give 1; each paired with 99997 gives the answer.
[99998,99998,99997]
=> 9999500006

# Every value the same.
[100000,100000,100000]
=> 1

# Duplicates of the largest value, and a 1 between them.
[100000,1,100000]
=> 100000

# Each value divides the next: the smallest and the largest give 81 / 3.
[3,9,27,81]
=> 27

# The best pair, 20 and 12, leaves out the two largest values.
[60,30,20,12]
=> 15

# Every value divides 100000.
[100000,50000,25000]
=> 4

# All multiples of 7000: 14000 and 21000 give 2 * 3.
[7000,14000,21000]
=> 6

# Many copies of one value and one other value.
[4,4,4,6]
=> 6

# The pair with the smallest gcd isn't the best: 2 and 3 are the only
# coprime pair (6), but 2 and 18 give 9.
[2,3,12,18]
=> 9

# Paired with 12, the strength first falls (8 gives 6, then 6 gives 2) and
# then rises: 12 and 5 give 60.
[8,5,12,6]
=> 60

[11,11]
=> 1

[5,5,3,1,5,2,2,3]
